title: K P B V Kumar , Junia Kumar, Karimnagar ... vs M Sabitha, Ranga Reddy Dist on 19 January, 2026

paragraphs.text:
HIGH COURT FOR THE STATE OF TELANGANA
 AT HYDERABAD
 HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE K. LAKSHMAN
 AND
 HON'BLE JUSTICE VAKITI RAMAKRISHNA REDDY

 FAMILY COURT APPEAL No.136 OF 2015

Date:19.01.2026

Between

XXXXXXX ....Appellant

 and

XXXXXXX ......Respondent

This Court passed the following

 JUDGMENT:

(Per Hon'ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman)


 Heard Sri Telugu Amarnath, learned counsel representing

Sri B. Nalin Kumar, learned counsel appearing for the respondent.

2. Despite service of notice, there is no representation on behalf

of the appellant.

3. Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied with the order dated

20.03.2014 passed in FCOP No.311 of 2012 by the Judge, Family

Court, at Secunderabad, the appellant - husband preferred the present
 2



appeal. Vide the said order, the Judge, Family Court, dismissed the

said FCOP.

4. The appellant - husband filed FCOP No.311 of 2012 under

Section 3 (ix) and (x) of the Indian Divorce Act, 1869 (for short, 'the

Act, 1869') against his wife seeking dissolution of marriage on the

grounds of cruelty and desertion alleging that respondent -wife is an

adamant and headstrong person. She started ill-treating him under one

pretext or the other. She sold away household articles, pattu sarees,

gold ornaments purchased by him and, rice etc., to help her parents.

She used to misbehave and abuse him in filthy language in front of his

friends and guests when they visit his house and she did not even

prepare food for him causing mental agony to him. She is frigid and

used to deny his company. She sent him scandalous and defamatory

messages in respect of his character and reputation. Since 2005, in

spite of his attempts, she did not join him. She used to visit his

workplace to defame him. She is highly educated and has a good

source of income. There is no chance of re-union as she had deserted

him since 2005. She also filed a petition under Section 125 of

Cr.P.C., seeking maintenance vide M.C.No.72 of 2005, a petition

under Section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (for short, 'the
 3
 DV Act ') vide DVC No.13 of 2009 and also a complaint under

 Section 498-A of IPC. Thus, the respondent subjected him to cruelty.

5. The respondent - wife filed counter opposing the allegations

made by the husband against her and sought to dismiss the petition.

6 To prove the said cruelty and desertion, the appellant -

husband examined himself as P.W.1, B.Arun Madhav, DGM Legal

and Nodal Officer, Idea Cellular for Andhra Pradesh as P.W.2 and

filed Ex.A.1 - copies of a bunch of messages (SMSs).
7. To disprove the claim of the appellant - husband, respondent

- wife, examined herself as R.W.1 and filed copy of judgment in DVC

No.13 of 2009, dated 15.06.2012 as Ex.B.1 and certified copy of

vakalat filed by appellant in Crl.A.No.558 of 2012 as Ex.B.2.

8. In the light of the above facts, the following points fell for

consideration before the Judge, Family Court:-
1. Whether the appellant - husband is entitled for divorce?
2. To what relief?

9. On consideration of the evidence on record, both oral and

documentary, vide impugned order dated 20.03.2014, the learned

Judge, Family Court, on elaborate discussion, gave a specific finding
 4



that the appellant - husband failed to prove cruelty and desertion and

dismissed the petition filed by him seeking dissolution of marriage.

10. It is the specific contention of the appellant that the

respondent - wife subjected him to cruelty by filing series of cases

against him and also deserted him for no fault of him.

11. It is the specific contention of the respondent - wife that she

never subjected the appellant to cruelty. She was constrained to file

cases against him as he subjected her to cruelty and neglected her and

her children to maintain.

12. In view of the above rival contentions, perusal of the record

would reveal that the marriage of the appellant with the respondent

took place on 20.06.2003 as per Christian rites and customs. They

were blessed with two daughters. Both of them became majors. The

appellant was correspondent in Arora College of Education. The

respondent was a private employee. The respondent has filed an

application vide M.C.No.72 of 2005 under Section 125 of Cr.P.C,

against the appellant - husband seeking maintenance and the same

was allowed. She has also lodged a complaint against the appellant for

the offence under Section 498-A of IPC and the Police Jagtial,

registered a crime and on completion of investigation, laid charge
 5



sheet against the appellant - husband. He was convicted by the trial

Court. Aggrieved by the said judgment, the appellant preferred

Crl.A.No.558 of 2012. She has also filed an application under Section

12 of the DV Act, vide DVC No.13 of 2009 and the same was also

allowed. Filing a petition under Section 12 of the DV Act, petition

under Section 125 of Cr.P.C, and a complaint for the offence under

 Section 428- A of IPC, does not constitute cruelty.

13. The appellant - husband who filed the aforesaid petitions

seeking dissolution of marriage on the grounds of cruelty and

desertion has to plead and prove the same by producing convincing

and cogent evidence. On mere allegations, he cannot seek divorce.

14. It is also relevant to note that the Supreme Court in Samar

Ghosh v. Jaya Ghosh1 observed that human mind is extremely

complex and human behaviour is equally complicated. Similarly

human ingenuity has no bound; therefore, to assimilate the entire

human behaviour in one definition is almost impossible. What is

cruelty in one case may not amount to cruelty in other case. The

concept of cruelty differs from person to person depending upon his

upbringing, level of sensitivity, educational, family and cultural

1
 (2007) 4 SCC 511
 6



background, financial position, social status, customs, traditions,

religious beliefs, human values and their value system.

15. In Rakesh Raman v. Smt. Kavita 2, the Apex Court

observed that Matrimonial cases before the Courts pose a different

challenge, quite unlike any other, as we are dealing with human

relationships with its bundle of emotions, with all its faults and

frailties. It is not possible in every case to pinpoint to an act of cruelty

or blameworthy conduct of the spouse. The nature of relationship, the

general behaviour of the parties towards each other, or long separation

between the two is relevant factors which a Court must take into

consideration.

16. In Naveen Kohli v. Neelu Kohli 3, the Apex Court held that

cruelty is a course or conduct of one, which is adversely affecting the

other. The cruelty may be mental or physical, intentional or

unintentional. The cruelty alleged may largely depend upon the type

of life the parties are accustomed to or their economic and social

conditions and their culture and human values which they attach

importance. Each case has to be decided on its own merits.

2
 2023 AIR (SC 2144
3
 (2006) 4 SCC 558
 7

17. Cruelty is not defined in any statute. It is a course or

conduct of one, which is adversely affecting the other. We have to

consider the entire evidence and the allegations made by the husband,

assess the same and come to a conclusion as to whether it amounts to

cruelty or not. In the present case, the evidence on record would reveal

that the appellant -husband failed to make out a case that he was

subjected by the respondent - wife to cruelty and also deserted him.

The impugned order is a reasoned order and well founded. It does not

require interference by this Court.

18. In the light of the aforesaid discussion, this appeal is liable

to be dismissed and is dismissed. There shall be no order as to costs.

Consequently, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this
appeal shall stand closed.
